risk_plain_language: Two or more strongly anticholinergic medicines raise the risk of confusion and memory problems
Three or more medicines that act on the brain raise the risk of falls and fractures

Two blood thinners (anticoagulants) taken together sharply raise the risk of serious bleeding. This is usually not intended (for example, an old prescription that was never stopped when a new one started), so a clinician should confirm which one the patient should be taking.
source: ELIQUIS (apixaban) prescribing information, 5.2 Bleeding: concomitant use of drugs affecting hemostasis, including other anticoagulants, increases the risk of bleeding
